chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Bilal al-Mahlabi reported to me, he said: Ali ibn Abdillah ibn Asad al-Isfahani narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us, he said: Ismail ibn Aban narrated to us, he said: al-Sabbah ibn Yahya al-Muzani narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abbad ibn Abdillah, who said:

A man came to Amirul Mu'mineen, peace be upon him, and said: 'O Amirul Mu'mineen, explain to me the verse of Allah the Exalted: Is then the one who stands upon a clear sign from his Lord, and a witness from him follows him?'

He (Ali) said: 'The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, is the one who stood on a clear sign from his Lord, and I am the witness for him and from Him. By He Who controls my soul, there is no one from Quraysh over whom the razors have passed except that Allah has revealed a portion of His Book concerning him. By He Who controls my soul, that the people would know what Allah has destined for us, the Ahl al-Bayt, through the tongue of the unlettered Prophet, is more beloved to me than having this entire courtyard filled with gold. By Allah, our example in this Ummah is none other than like Noah’s Ark, and like the Gate of Hittah (Forgiveness) for the Children of Israel.'

key_terms.المواسي: Al-Mawasi - Razors; an expression meaning 'every adult male from Quraysh' (those who have reached the age of shaving)
key_terms.باب حطة: Bab Hittah - The Gate of Forgiveness from the story of Bani Israel (Quran 2:58), a metaphor for spiritual purification through Ahlul Bayt
key_terms.بينة: Bayyinah - Clear proof or sign from God, here referring to divine guidance
key_terms.سفينة نوح: Safinat Nuh - Noah's Ark, a metaphor for the salvific role of Ahlul Bayt
key_terms.شاهد: Shahid - Witness, here interpreted as Imam Ali (AS) bearing witness to the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Who is the witness in Quran 11:17 according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of Sheikh al-Mufid, Imam Ali (AS) interprets Quran 11:17, identifying the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) as the one upon a clear sign from his Lord, and himself as the witness. This was a well-known interpretation in Shia exegesis, used to establish the divinely mandated role of Ali (AS) as the Prophet's successor. Ali (AS) further emphasizes the status of Ahlul Bayt by comparing them to Noah's Ark—whoever boards is saved—and to the Gate of Hittah in the story of the Children of Israel, through which whoever entered was forgiven.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 5. He said: Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn Bilal al-Mahlabi reported to me from ‘Ali ibn Abdillah ibn Asad al-Ishfahani, who reported from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who reported from Ismail ibn Aban, who reported from al-Sabbah ibn Yahya al-Muzni, from al-A’mash from al-Minhal ibn Amru, from Abbad ibn Abdillah, who said:

That a person called upon Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, and asked: "O Amirul Mu’mineen, explain to me the verse of Qur’an in which Allah says: ’Is the one who stands upon a clear sign from his Sustainer and a witness to him follows him ....?’ (Hud, 11:17)

He (‘Ali) said: "The messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his progeny, is the one who stood on a clear sign from His Sustainer; and I am his witness from Him. By He Who controls my breath, Allah has mentioned in His Book about every group from Quraish. By Him Who controls my soul, for the people to understand what Allah has destined for us Ahlul Bayt, through the revelation to His unlearned Prophet, is more lovable to me than for me to have the whole expanse filled with gold. By Allah, our example in this Ummah is like Noah’s Arc or like the Gate of Forgiveness for the children of Israel."
